items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: Sandy and I were very good friends even when I was a Kid kidding around Washington, you know.

ctx.x: And I went with Earl instead because of Jimmy Mundy was there. And, you know, I knew what he's going to write, and I -- the things he wrote. And I enjoyed his arrangements. And I didn't know any -- I didn't -- wasn't familiar with a lot of the guys with Chick. The guy who wanted me with Chick's band bad was from Washington, and he's a trombone player. It was Sandy Williams.

Sandy and I were very good friends even when I was a Kid kidding around Washington, you know. And he used to always encourage me. In fact, he tried to get me with Fletcher once but I wouldn't go, you know. Because when I was with Earl, it was kind of hard to get me away because I just dug the guys. I dug Budd, and I dug Ray Nance, and Walter Fuller and I were good friends. George Dickson and I -- Wally Bishop --

we all were just real good friends. It wasn't a matter of money because none of them were paying much money. The only bands them that probably was paying more money would be a band like Cab or Duke. You know, those were the only ones in -- I didn't want to work with Cab. He had a lot of good men with him but I always felt -- I could have been wrong -- but I always felt that he didn't give the guys a chance to actually do what they could do.
